title: cladebreaker pipeline parameters
description: implementation of the Planet Lab cladebreaker pipeline.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/cladebreaker/usage#samplesheet-input).

outdir.description: Path to the output directory where the results will be saved.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

proteins.description: Path to Genbank file for use during annotation.  See Prokka documentation for appropriate formatting.

prodigal_tf.description: Path to pretrained prodigal model file for use during annotation.  See Prokka documentation for appropriate formatting.

o.description: Specifies that precompressed WhatsGNU database is ortholog.

b.description: Specifies that precompressed WhatsGNU database is basic.

topgenomes_count.description: Number of topgenomes for WhatsGNU to find.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

ref.help_text: This parameter is *mandatory* if using a reference based alignment.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

max_job_request_options.title: Max job request options
max_job_request_options.description: Set the top limit for requested resources for any single job.
max_job_request_options.help_text:
If you are running on a smaller system, a pipeline step requesting more resources than are available may cause the Nextflow to stop the run with an error. These options allow you to cap the maximum resources requested by any single job so that the pipeline will run on your system.

Note that you can not _increase_ the resources requested by any job using these options. For that you will need your own configuration file. See [the nf-core website](https://nf-co.re/usage/configuration) for details.

max_cpus.description: Maximum number of CPUs that can be requested for any single job.
max_cpus.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the CPU requirement for each process. Should be an integer e.g. `--max_cpus 1`

max_memory.description: Maximum amount of memory that can be requested for any single job.
max_memory.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the memory requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_memory '8.GB'`

max_time.description: Maximum amount of time that can be requested for any single job.
max_time.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the time requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_time '2.h'`

shovill_options.title: Shovill input options
shovill_options.description: Shovill specific options, useful for customizing the assembly step of the pipeline.
shovill_options.help_text: These options are specific to Shovill. For customization of these options, see the Shovill readme on Github.

shovill_depth.help_text: Use to set a value other than default for Shovill depth.

shovill_gsize.help_text: Use to set estimated genome size for Shovill. No input sets autodetect (default),=.

build_options.title: cladebreaker build options
build_options.description: Options for the `cladebreaker build` workflow (entry: CLADEBREAKER_BUILD). Used to automatically download or construct a WhatsGNU database for a target species.
build_options.help_text: These parameters are only relevant when running the database build workflow via `nextflow run main.nf -entry CLADEBREAKER_BUILD` or through the interactive `cladebreaker_build.py` script. They are not used by the main analysis pipeline.

taxid.description: NCBI TaxID of the target species for database construction.
taxid.help_text: Provide the NCBI Taxonomy ID for the species you want to build a WhatsGNU database for (e.g. 1280 for Staphylococcus aureus). The build workflow will query NCBI Assembly for all available genomes under this TaxID, download them, annotate with Prokka, and compress them into a WhatsGNU database.

genome_count.description: Maximum number of reference genomes to include in the database build.
genome_count.help_text: Limits the number of genomes downloaded from NCBI for the custom build. Genomes are selected in the order returned by NCBI Assembly. If not set, all available assemblies for the given TaxID are used.

download_chunk_size.help_text: The accession list is split into chunks of this size and each chunk downloaded as its own job, so a failure retries only that chunk rather than the whole set.

download_forks.help_text: NCBI throttles aggressive clients with HTTP 503s. Lower this if downloads keep failing; raise it only on a connection you know NCBI tolerates.

download_max_retries.description: Retries per chunk when a download fails from throttling.

db_mode.description: WhatsGNU database mode to build: 'basic' or 'ortholog'.
db_mode.help_text:
Controls which compression mode WhatsGNU uses when building the database.

- **basic**: Compresses all proteins across all genomes. Suitable for any species. Recommended default.
- **ortholog**: Groups proteins by ortholog clusters before compression. Provides additional rarity scoring but requires a well-sampled reference set.

The resulting database mode must match the `--o` (ortholog) or `--b` (basic) flag used when running the main cladebreaker pipeline.

annotator.description: Genome annotation tool to use: 'prokka' (default) or 'bakta'.
annotator.help_text:
Selects the annotation tool used to predict protein-coding genes from downloaded reference genomes before building the WhatsGNU database.

- **prokka**: Fast, widely-used prokaryotic annotator. No database required.
- **bakta**: More accurate annotation using a curated database. Requires `--bakta_db` to point to a local Bakta database (download with `bakta_db download`).

bakta_db.description: Path to a local Bakta database directory. Required when --annotator bakta is set.
bakta_db.help_text:
Path to a pre-downloaded Bakta database. Download with:

```
bakta_db download --output /path/to/db
```

Only used when `--annotator bakta` is specified.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

tracedir.description: Directory to keep pipeline Nextflow logs and reports.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

show_hidden_params.help_text: By default, parameters set as _hidden_ in the schema are not shown on the command line when a user runs with `--help`. Specifying this option will tell the pipeline to show all parameters.

enable_conda.description: Run this workflow with Conda. You can also use '-profile conda' instead of providing this parameter.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

force.description: Nextflow will overwrite existing output files.

workflow.description: Which workflow to run: unset for the main pipeline, or 'BUILD' / 'ANALYZE'.
workflow.help_text: Selects the pipeline entry point. Leave unset to run the main cladebreaker analysis. `BUILD` constructs a WhatsGNU database from NCBI; `ANALYZE` runs statistics on an existing tree.

analyze_options.title: cladebreaker analyze options
analyze_options.description: Options for the `cladebreaker analyze` workflow (--workflow ANALYZE) and for running the same statistics on the tree built by the main pipeline.
analyze_options.help_text:
The genealogical sorting index (gsi) of Cummings, Neel & Shaw (2008) quantifies how far each labeled group on a rooted tree has sorted towards exclusive ancestry, from 0 (ancestry fully mixed with the other groups) to 1 (monophyletic). Significance comes from permuting the group labels across the tips.

Run it standalone on any rooted tree with `--workflow ANALYZE --tree <tree.nwk> --groups <groups.tsv>`, or add `--run_gsi` to a normal pipeline run to score your isolates against the reference genomes WhatsGNU selected.

tree.description: Newick tree to analyze, or a file of several trees for an ensemble gsi.
tree.help_text:
A single Newick tree, or a file holding one tree per line (RAxML-NG bootstrap replicates, or a posterior sample). With more than one tree the ensemble statistic gsi_T is reported, weighting each topology by its frequency in the sample.

Required for `--workflow ANALYZE`.

groups.description: Two-column table (TSV or CSV) mapping each tip label to a group name.
groups.help_text:
One row per tip, with an optional header:

```
tip_label\tgroup
SAMPLE_1\tquery
GCA_000012345.1\treference
```

At least two groups are needed. Tips left out of the file are rejected unless `--gsi_ignore_unlabeled` is set.

Required for `--workflow ANALYZE`. The main pipeline builds this file itself when `--run_gsi` is used.

run_gsi.description: Run the genealogical sorting index on the RAxML-NG tree built by the pipeline.
run_gsi.help_text: Requires `--run_raxml`. Labels your input isolates as one group and the reference genomes downloaded from NCBI as another, then scores how far each group has sorted. Results land in `<outdir>/gsi/` and in the MultiQC report.

tests.description: Which tests to run: 'auto' (all of them), or a comma-separated subset.
tests.help_text:
Valid names are gsi, monophyly, rosenberg, slatkin_maddison and snp_separation.

Under the default `auto` every test runs and the report decides which result leads: Rosenberg's chance-monophyly test where the groups are clades, Slatkin-Maddison's migration test where they are not. Running them all costs very little next to building the tree, and keeps every intermediate available.

`snp_separation` needs `--alignment` or `--distances`; under `auto` it is skipped when neither is given, but naming it explicitly without one is an error.

alignment.description: Core alignment, used to compute SNP distances for the separation test.
alignment.help_text: snp-dists is run over this to build a pairwise SNP distance matrix. In the main pipeline the alignment is taken automatically from whichever mode ran (the core-gene alignment in pangenome mode, or snippy-core's in reference mode).

distances.description: A precomputed snp-dists matrix, used instead of --alignment.

run_analysis.description: Run the full analyze decision path on the tree built by the pipeline.
run_analysis.help_text: Requires `--run_raxml`. Runs monophyly, Rosenberg, the gsi, Slatkin-Maddison and SNP separation on your isolates against the reference genomes WhatsGNU selected, then writes a combined report to `<outdir>/analyze/`. Supersedes `--run_gsi`, which runs the genealogical sorting index alone.

gsi_alpha.description: Significance level used by the report and by Rosenberg's minimum sample size.

gsi_max_joint_groups.description: Skip the joint monophyly probability beyond this many groups.
gsi_max_joint_groups.help_text: The joint probability of Zhu, Degnan & Steel (2011) sums over rooted binary trees on k leaves. It is evaluated by recursion over subsets, which is O(3^k), so it stays tractable well past the (2k-3)!! trees a naive enumeration would need -- but not indefinitely. Per-group P_A is unaffected and is always reported.

no_report.description: Skip rendering the PDF report. `--no-report` is accepted too.
no_report.help_text:
The analyze workflow writes a PDF containing the rooted tree the statistics were computed on, followed by each test's results. Pass this to skip it and keep only the text, TSV and JSON outputs.

The figure draws the tree written by the `monophyly` test, so the PDF is skipped automatically when `--tests` does not select it.

gsi_root.description: How to root the tree: 'as-is', 'midpoint' or 'outgroup'.
gsi_root.help_text:
The gsi is undefined on an unrooted tree, and a mis-rooted tree still produces plausible-looking values, so the rooting is always an explicit choice.

- **as-is**: trust the Newick as written. Correct when the tree is already rooted.
- **midpoint**: root at the midpoint of the longest tip-to-tip path. Needs branch lengths.
- **outgroup**: root on the clade named by `--gsi_outgroup`.

RAxML-NG output is unrooted, so `midpoint` or `outgroup` is normally what you want for a tree straight out of the pipeline.

gsi_outgroup.description: Comma-separated tip labels to root on. Required when --gsi_root outgroup.
gsi_outgroup.help_text: One or more tip labels, e.g. `GCA_000012345.1` or `GCA_000012345.1,GCA_000067890.1`. The tree is rooted on the branch subtending their most recent common ancestor, so the outgroup should be monophyletic.

gsi_permutations.description: Number of label permutations used to estimate the p-value.
gsi_permutations.help_text:
The observed labeling counts as one replicate, so the default of 9999 gives the 10^4 replicates used in the original paper. Set to 0 to skip the significance test and report the gsi alone.

Precision of the p-value is set by this number; 9999 permutations on a 100-tip tree take a couple of seconds.

gsi_seed.description: Random seed for the permutation test, so runs are reproducible.

gsi_groups_to_test.description: Comma-separated subset of group names to report (default: all groups).

gsi_ignore_unlabeled.description: Allow tree tips that carry no group label; they stay on the tree but take no part in the statistic.
gsi_ignore_unlabeled.help_text: Unlabeled tips still contribute to the tree topology, and so to min(gs), but are not counted as members of any group and are not permuted. Without this flag a tip missing from the groups file is an error.

gsi_query_label.description: Group name given to the input isolates when --run_gsi builds the groups file.

gsi_reference_label.description: Group name given to the downloaded reference genomes when --run_gsi builds the groups file.
